cell.contract_basis: exit_map.1: a declared source differs or is missing/nonregular at candidate

rules: trusted unresolvable or trusted path missing/nonregular -> 2 UNAVAILABLE
candidate entry mode not in {100644,100755} or type != blob -> 1 DRIFT
blob content differs from trusted -> 1 DRIFT else 0 BOUND
oracle.self_test: first run mis-reported class 'missing' as exit 2; caught by comparing all six classes to the frozen counter expectation table; fixed (entry() now distinguishes bad-commit from absent-path)

findings: expected=1 and token EXECUTOR_SOURCE_DRIFT for symlink are faithful to contract exit_map.1; grading is exit-equality plus token substring in combined stdout/stderr

dangling relative symlink (tools/elsewhere.py absent) stores cleanly as mode 120000 blob under counter env; even a hypothetical core.symlinks=false leak would keep this cell's expected outcome (content differs -> DRIFT)

coverage note: symlink blob content 'elsewhere.py' differs from trusted blob, so pure-content-comparing tools also exit 1; this cell does not by itself force mode inspection, but does catch existence-only tools

sharpest edge: a tool resolving the symlink via the working tree hits ENOENT and may emit exit 2; contract mandates DRIFT (exit 1) for nonregular-at-candidate, so the counter failing such a tool is correct
fixture worktree remains at the symlink commit for all 24 runs; worktree-keyed tools misjudge this path's other classes by design and are caught
git cat-file -t reports 'blob' for the symlink object; only ls-tree/ls-files mode 120000 reveals nonregularity
ls-tree quotes the non-ASCII path (core.quotepath); counter passes path via argv which round-trips (surrogateescape, Python 3.14 UTF-8); parsing-hazard is tool-side only
config isolation verified: only .git/config visible inside fixture; unresolvable candidate 0*40 fails rev-parse with rc=1
